findings.title: Listed theory T omits the value-group data required for decidability transfer
findings.location: PDF p.9 Corollary 1.7.6 (TeX 390-394); p.37 Corollary 5.3.5 (TeX 1566-1573); p.34 Theorem 5.1.7 (TeX 1435-1440)
findings.source_claim: Perfect henselian characteristic-p models with algebraically maximal O[t^-1] and the same theory of O/(t) decide every Lval sentence as the tilt does.
findings.complete_check: K=Cp, E=Kflat with GammaE=Q and v(t)=1. F=E((z^Z[1/p])) with composite valuation has GammaF=Z[1/p] lex Q. F is perfect and henselian; the full Hahn coarse valuation is maximal, O_F[t^-1]=O_w, and O_F/(t)=O_E/(t). For prime ell!=p, divisibility by ell holds in Q and fails at (1,0) in GammaF. Thus both F and E satisfy listed T while disagreeing on an Lval sentence.
findings.counterevidence: F need not be rank-one perfectoid: T explicitly axiomatizes the larger class. Theorem5.1.7 itself includes the missing condition. This is not a counterexample to Corollary5.3.5.
findings.impact: The displayed proof-enumeration procedure fails for an Lval sentence because the listed T has models disagreeing on it. This invalidates the original derivation of the explicitly advertised decidability transfer in Corollaries 1.7.6/5.3.5: Major, limited to that contribution. The corrected proof is conditional on the stated AKE theorem. No counterexample to the corollary or to the main embedding/Fontaine-Wintenberger conclusions is claimed.
findings.repair_verification: For mixed characteristic add Th(GammaK,v(p)) on (GammaF,u(t)), choosing t with tilt quotient O_K/(p) and vflat(t)=v(p). Both quotient ring and pointed group are uniformly interpretable using the same K-theory oracle. All models then satisfy Theorem5.1.7 side conditions and decide exactly the tilt's Lval theory. Characteristic-p case is immediate from Kflat=K.
findings.known_issue_status: No explicit correction identified in limited current search; no exhaustive novelty assertion.

findings.title: Discriminant is a derivative norm, not its square
findings.location: PDFp18 Fact2.4.7 proof(iii)<->(iv), TeX715; signed convention p17
findings.complete_check: Over henselian Q7, X^3-2 is irreducible since cubes mod7 are0,1,6; a is an integral unit. With delta=3a^2, delta^2=18a, while the manuscript's signed discriminant and Norm(delta) are108, unequal since a notin Q7. Exact SymPy determinant/resultant/remainder checks exit0.
findings.counterevidence: Authors' sign convention respected; ordinary discriminant is-108. Both delta and discriminant are units in this example, so it does not refute the unramifiedness criterion.
findings.impact: False local identity; subsequent inspected uses require the valid unit criterion, not equality to a square.
findings.repair_verification: Replace by disc(m_a)=Norm(m_a'(a)); uniqueness of henselian valuation gives v(disc)=degree*v'(derivative), hence unit iff unit.
findings.known_issue_status: Limited correction search; no identified correction.

findings.title: Example5.3.2 distinguishing element fails at p=2
findings.source_claim: p^(1/p) is absent from completed Qp(zeta_p-infinity), with no odd-prime restriction.
findings.complete_check: For p2, zeta8 lies already in cyclotomic union and (zeta8+zeta8^-1)^2=2. Exact remainder of (z-z^3)^2-2 modulo z^4+1 is0. Both fields therefore satisfy exists x:x^2=2.
findings.counterevidence: No conclusion that the two fields are elementarily equivalent at p2; earlier p!=2 restriction belongs to another example.
findings.impact: One witness and prime boundary of an illustration fail; existence of different untilts remains supported for odd primes.
findings.repair_verification: Restrict this example argument to odd p. Eisenstein degree p extension Qp(p^(1/p)) is non-Galois since otherwise p-1 divides p; finite cyclotomic subextensions are abelian, and Krasner approximation prevents completion from adding new algebraic elements. No replacement p2 witness claimed.

independent_acceptance.reasoning: P1: for K=Cp and E=Kflat, the full Hahn field F=E((z^Z[1/p])) with the composite valuation is perfect and henselian; its coarse full Hahn valuation is maximal, O_u[t^-1]=O_w, and O_u/(t)=O_E/(t). E and F both model the stated T, but their value groups Q and Z[1/p] lex Q disagree on ell-divisibility for ell!=p. Thus neither the distinguishing sentence nor its negation follows from T, and the proposed proof enumeration fails. The same transfer guarantee is explicitly advertised as Corollary 1.7.6; this supports Major for its original derivation, independently of whether the headline embedding uses it. Adding the pointed value-group theory, interpretable from the same K-theory oracle, gives a valid repair conditional on the stated AKE theorem; the corollary itself is not refuted. P2: over Q7, X^3-2 gives derivative square 18a versus signed norm/discriminant 108, but the norm valuation restores precisely the unit criterion used downstream, so Minor. P3: zeta8+zeta8^-1 squares to 2, invalidating the p=2 witness; the odd-prime restriction follows by Eisenstein, non-Galois degree and Krasner, so Minor. No p=2 elementary equivalence or replacement witness is claimed.
independent_acceptance.correction: P1 and overall Minor -> Major, limited to the advertised decidability-transfer proof. P2/P3 remain Minor. Abstract, overview, impact paragraph, conclusion table, findings and coverage synchronized.
